h1: Pool and Spa Electrical in Broward County
intro: Water and electricity together demand special protection, and many older South Florida pools no longer have it. On a pool decades in the ground, the grounding, bonding, and ground fault breakers that keep swimmers safe can quietly fail while everything looks fine. A tripping breaker, a dark light, or a faint tingle on a rail is the warning. Our licensed crew tests instead of guesses and fixes the cause.

definition.heading: What pool and spa electrical work covers
definition.body: Pool and spa electrical covers everything on the electrical side of your pool: the pump and heater circuits, lighting, the salt system, the breakers, and the grounding and bonding that ties it together safely. Bonding keeps every metal part at the same electrical level so a swimmer feels no charge. Grounding gives a fault a safe path so the breaker trips.

symptoms.title: A tingle in the water
symptoms.body: Someone feels a faint buzz when they touch a rail, ladder, or light, and it fades when they let go. That is current reaching metal it should not, usually a broken bond, and the clearest warning there is, so get everyone out and have it checked.

symptoms.title: A pool breaker that keeps tripping
symptoms.body: A pump, heater, or light breaker keeps tripping, and resetting it only buys a little time. On a pool circuit that usually means the breaker is sensing a real ground fault and doing exactly its job.

symptoms.title: A pool light out or flickering
symptoms.body: Your pool light has gone dark, flickers, or trips its breaker when you switch it on. Because the light sits in the water, that is exactly where you want a correct repair rather than a quick guess.

symptoms.title: Your pool still runs on its original breakers
symptoms.body: The pool was built decades ago and still runs on its original breakers, or a new pump or heater went in on an old bond. Fast-tripping ground fault protection may never have been installed, or it has aged out and no longer trips as it should.

localSections.heading: Older South Florida pools, older services, deeper faults
localSections.body: Many South Florida pools date to the 1960s through the 1980s, and homes from West Palm Beach to North Miami Beach still have them. Bonding standards were looser then, and some used metal conduit as the ground path instead of a wire. Decades of humidity and coastal salt air corrode the lugs, and none of it shows from the deck.

localSections.heading: Permits, inspection, and your insurance in Broward
localSections.body: Broward County building departments watch pool electrical work closely, which protects you. When a correction needs a permit, we pull it, work to current code, and meet the inspector to prove the grounding under test. Some minor fixes do not need one, and we say which is which. A closed permit documents that a licensed contractor handled the work correctly.

guide.title: The complete guide to pool and spa electrical

sections.heading: Bonding and grounding: two jobs, one safety net
sections.body: Bonding and grounding are two different jobs. Bonding ties every metal part around your pool, the rails, ladder, pump, heater, and light niche, into one connected network so a swimmer feels no difference in charge between two things they touch at once. Grounding gives fault current a fast path back so the breaker senses it and shuts off. The only way to tell a healthy system from a failed one is to test it.

sections.heading: A tripping breaker, and why a pool needs a different one
sections.body: On a pool circuit, a tripping breaker is sensing current escaping the wiring, so never reset it or fit a bigger one. Water lowers the body's resistance, so code calls for a ground fault breaker on the pump, heater, and lighting that compares the current leaving with what returns and trips the instant they do not match. A GFCI only protects if it trips, so we test every one before we leave.

sections.heading: When a repair becomes a rebuild
sections.body: Most pool problems are repairs we can fix on the spot. A rebuild is different: the signal is a pattern, not one fault, when you fix one circuit and another fails, the grounding was never right, and every look finds another violation. We once traced a community pool shocking swimmers to metal conduit used as its ground path, and ran new wire with a proper ground. When we touch it, we fix it completely.

faqs.question: What is the difference between bonding and grounding?
faqs.answer: Bonding ties all the metal around your pool into one network so everything sits at the same electrical level and a swimmer feels no difference in charge. Grounding gives fault current a safe path back so the breaker trips. A safe pool needs both, connected correctly.

faqs.question: My pool breaker keeps tripping. Can I just reset it or add a bigger one?
faqs.answer: Please do neither. On a pool circuit, a tripping breaker is usually sensing a real ground fault and shutting off before that current can reach a swimmer. A bigger breaker just lets more current flow before protection reacts, so let us find why it trips and fix the cause.

faqs.question: Someone felt a tingle in the pool. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Get everyone out and have it checked before the pool is used again. A tingle usually means current is reaching metal that is not properly bonded, and the swimmer becomes the path. We find the leak, restore the bond, and prove the breaker trips as it should.

faqs.question: How do I know if my pool already has proper ground fault protection?
faqs.answer: A ground fault breaker usually has a small test button, and pressing it should make the breaker trip. Plain breakers mean the circuits are likely on standard protection, and a breaker can also look correct yet have aged past reliable tripping. The only way to be sure is to test, which is part of what we do on a visit.
